title: Mitigate regional reroute storm and variant escalation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: On 2025-02-16 a sequence of noisy regional health signals triggered an aggressive reroute policy that drained a healthy subset of nodes in us-west-2, causing cross-tier misrouting and a cascading surge of fallback variant requests. The surge degraded tail latency for multiple hosted customers and increased token cost by ~3.7x for affected routes.

Timeline (condensed):
- 2025-02-16 03:07 UTC: regional health aggregator reported transient packet loss; the signal exceeded the reroute threshold due to a bug in smoothing logic.
- 03:09 UTC: routing controller started draining 12% of us-west-2 capacity toward regional fallback pool.
- 03:12 UTC: autoscaler misinterpreted drain as capacity pressure and triggered cross-tier promotion, swapping customers to smaller, higher-cost variants.
- 03:20 UTC: KV cache hit rate dropped for long-lived chat sessions; many in-flight requests were re-issued to fallback variants.
- 04:05 UTC: mitigation "circuit-hold" policy and manual rollback of drain tombstones restored normal routing.

Root cause: A regression in the regional signal smoothing code stopped applying the exponential decay window for brief packet-loss blips. This produced sustained high "unhealthy" scores for short incidents. Two weaknesses amplified the impact: (1) the reroute policy used a conservative hysteresis value that aggressively drained nodes at small deltas, and (2) autoscaler rule ENG-142839 treated drain velocity as an absolute capacity shortfall and promoted higher-cost model variants.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Reverted the smoothing regression (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4123).
- Throttled reroute actuation to require 15s sustained signal above threshold (temporary guard rails applied).
- Added a fast-rollback controller that stops drains if KV cache hit-rate drops >20% within 2 minutes of a drain.
- Manual rollback of variant promotions and reconciliation of cost-billing tags.

Postmortem analysis and long-term actions:
- Change reroute smoothing to use adaptive EWMA with confidence bands (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RR/Adaptive+Signal+Smoothing).
- Update reroute hysteresis to incorporate absolute capacity delta and route affinity weights instead of pure percentage thresholds.
- Tighten autoscaler semantics: decouple "drain velocity" from autoscale downscale decisions; autoscaler should only act on steady multi-minute capacity trending. (Follow-up ticket: ENG-218001)
- Introduce variant-cost throttles in routing layer to prevent automatic promotion to expensive variants when an upstream cache or disk pressure symptom is observed.
- Add synthetic canary that injects short packet-loss blips to validate smoothing and hysteresis behavior in staging.

Success criteria and telemetry:
- No more than 5% false-positive drains from transient signals in next 30 days.
- KV cache hit-rate regressions on route drains should be <5% and recover within 90s.
- Cost-surge alerts for variant promotions should trigger automated rollback within 3 minutes.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident timeline and raw traces: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/board/reroute-216789
- Fix PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4123, https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/256
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RR/Adaptive+Signal+Smoothing
- Postmortem notes and RCA meeting recording: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3C_reroute216789

Owners: Routing runtime lead (Mateo Rivera) responsible for smoothing and hysteresis changes; Autoscale team (lead: Priya Nair) to change policy semantics; QA to validate canary behavior.

Status: All immediate mitigations are merged and deployed to production; long-term items in backlog with owners and estimates.
